question: A 65-year-old man presents to the physician for the evaluation of increasing dyspnea and swelling of the lower extremities over the past year. He has no cough. He also complains of frequent awakenings at night and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has no history of a serious illness. He takes no medications other than zolpidem before sleep. He is a 35-pack-year smoker. His blood pressure is 155/95 mm Hg. His BMI is 37 kg/m2. Oropharyngeal examination shows a small orifice and an enlarged tongue and uvula. The soft palate is low-lying. The examination of the nasal cavity shows no septal deviation or polyps. Symmetric pitting edema is seen below the knee, bilaterally. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Echocardiography shows a mildly dilated right ventricle and an elevated systolic pulmonary artery pressure with no abnormalities of the left heart. A ventilation-perfusion scan shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient’s symptoms?

options.opb: Heart failure with a preserved ejection fraction

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "intermittent hypoxia" -> "pulmonary vasoconstriction" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> "dyspnea" -> "lower extremity edema" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "intermittent hypoxia" -> "daytime sleepiness" -> "frequent awakenings at night" -> "increased blood pressure" -> "right heart strain" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "upper airway obstruction" -> "increased negative intrathoracic pressure" -> "right heart strain" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "obesity" -> "increased neck circumference" -> "upper airway obstruction" -> "intermittent hypoxia" -> "pulmonary hypertension" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Idiopathic pulmonary artery hypertension" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> "dyspnea" -> "lower extremity edema" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Heart failure with a preserved ejection fraction" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> "dyspnea" -> "lower extremity edema" -> 50%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and findings are most consistent with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The key indicators include excessive daytime sleepiness, frequent awakenings at night, obesity (BMI of 37 kg/m2), and oropharyngeal examination findings of a small orifice, enlarged tongue, uvula, and low-lying soft palate. These are classic features of OSA, which can lead to pulmonary hypertension and right heart strain, as evidenced by the mildly dilated right ventricle and elevated systolic pulmonary artery pressure. The absence of left heart abnormalities and a normal ventilation-perfusion scan further support this diagnosis over other options.
